title: Practice · Money words without MBA
instructions: Answer one question at a time. Feedback appears after you submit.

questions.prompt: Maya sells one $79 guide. What is her revenue from that sale?

choices.text: Whatever cash hits her bank this week

questions.feedback: Revenue is the money customers pay you — here, $79.

questions.prompt: Revenue is $79 and cash cost is $3. What is profit before counting time?
You show a profit on paper, but the buyer has not paid yet. What might you still lack?
questions.feedback: Profit on paper is not the same as cash in hand.

questions.prompt: What is the primary learning objective of this lesson?

choices.text: Define revenue vs profit vs cash

questions.feedback: The lesson objective is: define revenue vs profit vs cash.

questions.prompt: Price is what the buyer pays. Margin is:
questions.feedback: Margin is what remains after the unit cost.

choices.text: Money in your account you can spend
A completed customer payment that cleared

questions.prompt: How do you know “Money words without MBA” landed?

choices.text: You can define revenue vs profit vs cash
You watched at 2× with captions off

questions.feedback: Competence is shown by doing the objective.

questions.prompt: After watching, your next step should be:

choices.text: Do the practice / quiz, then list costs for one unit of your offer

questions.feedback: Video pairs with practice — then apply the words to your offer.

application.prompt: For one unit of a simple digital product, write: price, estimated cost, profit, and when cash actually arrives.
